terms.definition: A global business strategy where multinational corporations diversify their supply chains beyond China to avoid over-reliance on a single country.
terms.simpleExplanation: Companies setting up backup factories in countries like India or Vietnam so they aren't completely dependent on Chinese factories.
terms.example: Apple expanding iPhone production lines across India and Vietnam alongside Chinese hubs.
terms.mbaRelevance: Crucial concept in Supply Chain Risk Management and Strategic Global Sourcing.

editorials.title: Boosting India's Manufacturing: Policy, Productivity, and Global Competition

terms.definition: A government scheme offering financial rewards to companies based on incremental sales from products manufactured in domestic units.
terms.simpleExplanation: A cash reward program from the government given to businesses that produce and sell more goods locally.
terms.example: Mobile phone manufacturers receiving a 4-6% financial incentive on additional phones produced in India.
terms.mbaRelevance: Demonstrates how public policy subsidies directly alter corporate CapEx strategy and unit economics.
